findings.passage: “House Republicans are trying to impose a pink poll tax on women in our state and undue burden on senior citizens and overseas service members,” said state Rep. Mai Xiong (D-Warren). “Mothers and previously married or divorced women should not have to spend their time and money on changing their documents to perform their rightful civic duty. I will not stand for a policy that risks making it harder for women in our state to vote.”
findings.note: Statement in her name at a press conference against House Joint Resolution B, which would require citizenship documents (birth certificate, passport or naturalization certificate) to vote; she objects on cost and name-mismatch grounds.
